I understand that now is not the right time.
But I wanted to talk about your mom.
What do you mean?
She is keeping me from working.
Vitya, what are you talking about?
Mom already died two years ago.
How, in what sense?
I told him back then.
He was in such a state that he forgot.

meanings.en: to sympathize with, feel for (with dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'очувствовать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'sympathize / offer condolences', paired with 'посочувствовать'.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я вам искренне сочувствую.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I sincerely sympathize with you.
I sympathize with him.
I sincerely feel for you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'здравлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'congratulations', paired with 'поздравить'.

examples.trans: Congratulations, you are the restaurant director.

examples.text: Поздравляю, а мне приходится работать с тупыми.
examples.trans: Congratulations, while I have to work with dull ones.
Congratulations on the promotion, Nikita.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thank you, Eleonora Andreyevna.
Thank you, I will stand.
Oh my goodness, thank you so much!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And you end up with six people.

examples.text: Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
examples.trans: You are our restaurant director, Ilya.
And Dmitry Vladimirovich's tailcoat.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'understand', paired with 'понять'.

examples.text: Катя, я понимаю, ты обижена на меня.
examples.trans: Katya, I understand you are upset with me.

examples.text: Я тебя понимаю, потому что я люблю тебя.
examples.trans: I understand you, because I love you.

examples.text: Я понимаю, что сейчас не вовремя.
examples.trans: I understand that now is not the right time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.
Why are we standing around?
What are you doing here?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: We will make new cookies right now.

examples.text: Я сам сейчас всё скажу Элеоноре.
examples.trans: I will tell Eleonora everything myself right now.

examples.text: Я понимаю, что сейчас не вовремя.
examples.trans: I understand that now is not the right time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.
Take it to my suite.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, вам повторять не надо.
examples.trans: I hope I do not need to repeat to you.

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

examples.text: Я понимаю, что сейчас не вовремя.
examples.trans: I understand that now is not the right time.
Bad timing!
He always comes on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.
Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.
Take it to my suite.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'wanted', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: Did you want to see me?

examples.text: Но я хотел поговорить про твою маму.
examples.trans: But I wanted to talk about your mom.
I want coffee.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

examples.text: Но я хотел поговорить про твою маму.
examples.trans: But I wanted to talk about your mom.
Talk to him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Let's go through the wedding script.

examples.text: Если пропадет омар, я тебя уволю.
examples.trans: If a lobster disappears, I will fire you.
Or did you simply miss me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я виновата, я вмешивалась в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I am at fault, I interfered in your life.

examples.text: Я никогда больше не буду лезть в твою жизнь.
examples.trans: I will never meddle in your life again.
Well you see, your Denis will be here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'Mama' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Катя говорила маме, что ты ей очень нравишься.
examples.trans: Katya told her mom that she likes you very much.
Mom, you look gorgeous.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.
And you end up with six people.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мысл'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sense, meaning' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: What do you mean?
How, in what sense?
There's no sense in it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Замуж она выходит не в моем кабинете.
examples.trans: She is not getting married in my office.

examples.text: Я приехал с супругой, а вот она.
examples.trans: I arrived with my wife, and here she is.
Yes, she pleaded for you.

meanings.en: to be in the way, to hinder
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'bothers', paired with 'помешать'.

examples.trans: She is keeping me from working.
The radiators are in the way.
Don't bother me!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Работать надо, а не моему мужу улыбаться.
examples.trans: You need to work, not smile at my husband.
Then who is going to run things today?

examples.text: Я все-таки с острыми предметами работаю.
examples.trans: After all, I work with sharp objects.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не знаю, помнишь ты или нет.
examples.trans: I do not know whether you remember or not.
You are fired.
You are fired!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.
They called and will definitely come.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'than', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: My presence is more than logical.
And why is it so expensive?
Why do you want to leave?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Одно ваше присутствие — это уже подарок.
examples.trans: Your presence alone is already a gift.

examples.text: Выручай, мне срочно нужен пианист на вечер.
examples.trans: Help me out, I urgently need a pianist for the evening.
And where is my betrothed?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'died', paired with 'умирать'.

examples.trans: She died last year.
He died very old.
But she died anyway.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'two', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мама уже умерла два года назад.
examples.trans: Mom already died two years ago.

examples.text: И у вас будет всего два постоянных гостя.
examples.trans: And you will have only two regular guests.
In two weeks.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'years' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Today is a very important banquet.
And what are you doing today?
Then who is going to run things today?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'back', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мама уже умерла два года назад.
examples.trans: Mom already died two years ago.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!
Five minutes ago.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: У вас ко мне какое-то дело?
examples.trans: Do you have some business with me?
What is her name?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('which').

examples.trans: You tell me how to do it.

examples.text: У вас ко мне какое-то дело?
examples.trans: Do you have some business with me?
What is her name?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'told', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Катя говорила маме, что ты ей очень нравишься.
examples.trans: Katya told her mom that she likes you very much.

examples.text: Я говорила, что я здесь ни при чем.
examples.trans: I told you that I had nothing to do with it.

examples.text: Катя из-за тебя поговорила с мамой.
examples.trans: Katya talked to her mom because of you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to him', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: They called and will definitely come.
Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.

examples.text: Замуж она выходит не в моем кабинете.
examples.trans: She is not getting married in my office.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Извините, можно у вас автограф взять?
examples.trans: Excuse me, may I get your autograph?
I told him back then.
Back then I was little.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'was'.

examples.trans: Maybe he left on his own?
I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You cannot act like this.

examples.text: Я все-таки с острыми предметами работаю.
examples.trans: After all, I work with sharp objects.
And why is it so expensive?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'остояние'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'condition / state' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он был в таком состоянии, что забыл.
examples.trans: He was in such a state that he forgot.
Checking the condition of the wall.
In good condition.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.text: Он был в таком состоянии, что забыл.
examples.trans: He was in such a state that he forgot.
Don't forget to wash the toilet.
I forgot the keys.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
examples.trans: An oligarch will be sitting at our table.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.
And you end up with six people.
